title: Hedging and Diplomacy in Academic Discussion / Atụziri na ndoro n'ulo akademia
bridge: Na English akademia, atụziri bụ nke a na-eme ka mmadụ na-eme ka ha dị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ ma ọ bụrụ na ha na-akwado. N'ime Spanish, ndị a na-eji subjunctive ka ha tụọrọ (n'ụzọ dịka 'Quizás sea cierto'), English na-eji verb modals (might, may, could) tụọrọ na adverb nke ụfọdụ na verb nke ndoro. N'ime error ndị a na-eme bụ ịbụ n'ọnọdụ doro anya, dịka n'ime Spanish 'Eso no es correcto', n'ime English o na-eme ka ọ dị mfe nke ọtụtụ ma ọ bụrụ na ọ bụ 'That might not be entirely accurate'. Nke ọzọ bụ n'ihi na ndị a na-eme mmemme 'suggest' na 'sugerir' n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na 'proponer', mana n'ime English 'suggest' na-eji tụọrọ na-enweghị ike ịmalite. Nke ọzọ bụ n'ihi na ndị a na-eme mmemme 'suggest' na 'sugerir' n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na 'proponer', mana n'ime English 'suggest' na-eji tụọrọ na-enweghị ike ịmalite.
rule: Atụziri n'ime English akademia na-eme ka ọ dị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ ma ọ bụrụ na ọ bụ: 1) Verb modals nke ịgụ maka ụfọdụ: might, may, could (n'ụzọ dịka 'This might indicate...'). 2) Verb nke ndoro n'ime ọtụtụ ndoro: I would argue, I tend to think, I feel. 3) Adverb nke ụfọdụ/ụfọdụ: perhaps, possibly, arguably, seemingly, apparently. 4) Verb nke report (reporting verbs) na-eme ka ha tụọrọ: suggests, indicates, implies, appears (n'ihi na 'proves' ma ọ bụ 'shows'). 5) Nkọmfe ndoro: it could be argued that, it seems that, one might consider. 6) Mmemme na adjectives: not entirely, not necessarily, not wholly (n'ụzọ dịka 'not entirely convincing'). 7) Iji 'somewhat', 'rather', 'fairly' n'efu na adjectives (n'ụzọ dịka 'somewhat controversial'). 8) Conditional nke hypothesis: if this were the case, it would... Nkọmfe ndoro: adịghị iji 'must' ma ọ bụ 'definitely' n'ulo akademia (ọ na-eme ka ha dị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ); adịghị iji 'very' (jiri 'highly', 'considerably'); na ịghọta na n'ime Spanish 'creo que' adịghị n'ụzọ dị n'ime 'I think' n'ime English, mana n'ime ụlọ akademia, 'I would argue' ma ọ bụ 'It seems to me' na-eji tụọrọ. Nkịtị: n'ime ndoro ndoro (n'ụzọ dịka 'This demonstrates...'), mana n'ihi na ọ bụ tụọrọ na-eme ka ha dị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ ma ọ bụrụ na ọ tụọrọ na 'strongly suggests'.

concept_examples.text: It could be argued that the author's conclusion is somewhat premature.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ tụọrọ na ndoro ndoro nke onye a na-akpọrọ bụ nke a na-eme ka ọ dị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ.
concept_examples.phonetic: ɪt kʊd bi ˈɑːrɡjuːd ðæt ði ˈɔːθərz kənˈkluːʒən ɪz ˈsʌmwʌt ˌpriːməˈtjʊr.

concept_examples.text: This evidence might suggest a different interpretation of the data.
concept_examples.translation: Nke a na-akpọrọ bụ na-eme ka ụfọdụ ndoro tụọrọ n'ụzọ ọzọ nke data.
concept_examples.phonetic: ðɪs ˈɛvɪdəns maɪt səˈdʒɛst ə ˈdɪfərənt ɪntərprɪˈteɪʃən əv ðə ˈdeɪtə.

concept_examples.text: I would argue that the methodology is not entirely valid.
concept_examples.translation: A tụọrọ na m na-akpọrọ na method nke a adịghị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ.
concept_examples.phonetic: aɪ wʊd ˈɑːrɡjuː ðæt ðə ˌmɛθəˈdɒlədʒi ɪz nɒt ɪnˈtaɪərli ˈvælɪd.

concept_examples.text: One might consider the possibility of a sampling bias.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ tụọrọ na ụfọdụ ndoro nke sampling bias.
concept_examples.phonetic: wʌn maɪt kənˈsɪdər ðə ˌpɒsəˈbɪlɪti əv ə ˈsæmplɪŋ ˈbaɪəs.

common_error.wrong: That's not true, you are wrong.
common_error.correct: That might not be entirely accurate.
common_error.correct_alt: I would respectfully disagree with that point.
common_error.explanation: N'ime error a na-eme bụ n'ihi na ndị a na-eme translation na Spanish 'Eso no es cierto, estás equivocado'. N'ime ụlọ akademia n'ime English, nke a na-akpọrọ bụ na-eme ka ọ dị mfe nke ọtụtụ ma ọ bụrụ na ọ bụ n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ na ọ bụrụ na ọ doro anya. N'ime Spanish, ndị a na-eji ndoro tụọrọ, mana nkọmfe grammar na-enyere ndị a ịbụ n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ. Iji tụọrọ n'ime English, a na-eme atụziri: tụọrọ na-eme ka ọ dị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ ma ọ bụrụ na ọ tụọrọ na 'might not' na-eme ka ha adịghị tụọrọ ndoro ndoro ('you are wrong') ma tụọrọ n'ide ('not accurate'). Nke ọzọ bụ iji condicional 'would' na verb 'disagree' tụọrọ na adverb dịka 'respectfully'.

examples.original: This theory might explain the observed phenomena.
examples.phonetic: ðɪs ˈθɪəri maɪt ɪkˈspleɪn ði əbˈzɜːvd fəˈnɒmɪnə.
examples.translation: Nke a na-akpọrọ bụ nwere ike ịmalite n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ. 'Might' tụọrọ na ụfọdụ ndoro. N'ime Spanish, 'podría' tụọrọ, mana ịghọta na 'may' adịghị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ ma ọ bụrụ na ọ dị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ.
examples.note: A na-eme 'might' n'ihi na ụfọdụ ndoro. N'ime Spanish, 'podría' tụọrọ, mana ịghọta na 'may' adịghị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ ma ọ bụrụ na ọ dị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ.

examples.original: The results could be interpreted in several ways.
examples.phonetic: ðə rɪˈzʌlts kʊd bi ɪnˈtɜːprɪtɪd ɪn ˈsɛvrəl weɪz.
examples.translation: Nke a tụọrọ bụ na-eme ka ha tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ. 'Could' tụọrọ na ụfọdụ ndoro, mana ọ adịghị n'ọnọdụ nke ọtụtụ. N'ime Spanish, 'poder' tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na 'can', mana n'ime English, 'could' tụọrọ na ụfọdụ ndoro ma ọ bụrụ na 'can' tụọrọ na ụfọdụ ndoro.
examples.note: 'Could' sugiere opciones, no certeza. En español el verbo 'poder' cubre ambos, pero en inglés 'could' es más hipotético que 'can'.

examples.original: These findings may indicate a need for further research.
examples.phonetic: ðiːz ˈfaɪndɪŋz meɪ ˈɪndɪkeɪt ə niːd fɔː ˈfɜːðər rɪˈsɜːtʃ.
examples.translation: Nke a tụọrọ bụ na-eme ka ha tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ. 'May' tụọrọ n'ụlọ akademia n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ na ụfọdụ ndoro. N'ime Spanish, 'pueden' adịghị tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na 'sugieren'.
examples.note: 'May' es común en escritura académica para sugerir una implicación sin afirmar. En español, 'pueden' no siempre se usa en este contexto; a veces se prefiere 'sugieren'.

levels.label: Reporting Verbs and Impersonal Structures
levels.translation: Verb nke report na nkọmfe ndoro

examples.original: The study suggests a correlation between sleep and memory.
examples.phonetic: ðə ˈstʌdi səˈdʒɛsts ə ˌkɒrəˈleɪʃən bɪˈtwiːn sliːp ænd ˈmɛməri.
examples.translation: Nke a tụọrọ bụ na-eme ka ha tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ. N'ime Spanish, 'sugiere' tụọrọ, mana n'ime English, ọ tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na 'shows'. tụọrọ 'proves' n'ime ụlọ akademia.
examples.note: N'ime Spanish, 'sugiere' tụọrọ, mana n'ime English, ọ tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na 'shows'. tụọrọ 'proves' n'ime ụlọ akademia.

examples.original: It could be argued that the sample size was insufficient.
examples.phonetic: ɪt kʊd bi ˈɑːrɡjuːd ðæt ðə ˈsæmpl saɪz wɒz ˌɪnsəˈfɪʃənt.
examples.translation: Ọ bụrụ na ọ tụọrọ na ndoro ndoro na ụfọdụ ndoro tụọrọ na ụfọdụ ndoro tụọrọ. N'ime Spanish, 'se podría argumentar' tụọrọ, mana ndị a tụọrọ na-eme ka ha tụọrọ 'it' ma tụọrọ 'podría argumentarse', mana ọ adịghị n'ime English.
examples.note: Esta estructura impersonal es clave. En español se usa 'se podría argumentar', pero muchos hablantes tienden a omitir 'it' y decir 'podría argumentarse', lo cual es incorrecto en inglés.

examples.original: It seems that the data are inconsistent with the hypothesis.
examples.phonetic: ɪt siːmz ðæt ðə ˈdeɪtə ɑːr ˌɪnkənˈsɪstənt wɪð ðə haɪˈpɒθɪsɪs.
examples.translation: Ọ tụọrọ na ụfọdụ ndoro tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ. 'It seems that' tụọrọ na ụfọdụ ndoro. N'ime Spanish, 'parece que' tụọrọ, mana n'ime English, nkọmfe 'it' tụọrọ.
examples.note: 'It seems that' es un atenuador fuerte. En español diríamos 'parece que', pero en inglés la estructura exige el sujeto 'it'.

examples.original: The argument is not entirely convincing.
examples.phonetic: ði ˈɑːrɡjumənt ɪz nɒt ɪnˈtaɪərli kənˈvɪnsɪŋ.
examples.translation: Nke a tụọrọ bụ na-eme ka ha tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ. N'ime Spanish, 'no del todo' tụọrọ, mana n'ime English, 'not entirely' tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na 'not very' tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ.
examples.note: En español usamos 'no del todo', y en inglés 'not entirely' es el equivalente exacto. Evita 'not very' que suena débil.

examples.original: This approach is rather problematic.
examples.phonetic: ðɪs əˈprəʊtʃ ɪz ˈrɑːðər ˌprɒbləˈmætɪk.
examples.translation: Nke a tụọrọ bụ na-eme ka ha tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ. 'Rather' n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na 'bastante' tụọrọ na ụfọdụ ndoro. N'ime Spanish, 'bastante' tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na 'very' tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ.
examples.note: 'Rather' en este contexto significa 'bastante' y suaviza la crítica. En español 'bastante' puede ser fuerte, pero en inglés 'rather' es más diplomático que 'very'.

examples.original: The results are somewhat surprising.
examples.phonetic: ðə rɪˈzʌlts ɑːr ˈsʌmwʌt səˈpraɪzɪŋ.
examples.translation: Nke a tụọrọ bụ na-eme ka ha tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ. 'Somewhat' tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na 'algo' ma ọ bụ 'un poco', mana n'ime English, ọ tụọrọ n'ụzọ dị n'ihi na ọ tụọrọ.
examples.note: 'Somewhat' equivale a 'algo' o 'un poco', pero en inglés se usa más formalmente. Úsalo para moderar afirmaciones.

title: Strategic Hedging & Diplomatic Language / Ntụgharị ndoro na Agụmaghị ndoro
bridge: N'igbo, okwukwe ndoro na-agụnye ndoro dị ka 'ọ bụ na', 'ọ bụ na ọ bụrụ na', ma ọ bụ nke ndoro nke nwere 'nwere', mana na English nke ndoro na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro dị ka 'perhaps', 'arguably' na ndoro ndoro dị ka 'seem', 'appear', 'tend to'. N'ime error nke ndoro nke a na-eme bụ ntụgharị okwukwe ndoro dị ka 'This is wrong' ma ọ bụ ntụgharị nke na-egosi 'It is possible that...' mgbe English nke ndoro na-elekwa modal ndoro dị ka 'might', 'may', 'could'. N'ihi na 'I think' na-eme ka okwukwe bụ ndoro dị ka 'I believe' n'ime English nke ndoro nwere 'nwere' nke ndoro nke ndoro nke a na-eme bụ 'creo' n'ime Spanish nwere nke ndoro nke ndoro.
rule: Ndoro ndoro (ndoro ndoro) n'ime English nke ndoro na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro dị ka: 1) Adverb ndoro: perhaps, possibly, arguably, presumably, allegedly (n'ime ma ọ bụ n'oge ndoro). 2) Verbs nke ndoro: seem, appear, tend to, suggest (na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro adịghị adị). 3) Modals: might, may, could (ndoro ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro). 4) Ntụgharị dị ka 'It could be argued that...', 'One might say that...' (na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro adịghị adị). 5) Adjectives: 'a bit', 'slightly', 'somewhat' (na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro adịghị adị). N'ime Spanish, okwukwe ndoro na-eme ka subjunctive na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro, mana n'ime English, okwukwe ndoro na-eme ka modal + form base (adịghị -s). Ej.: 'Es posible que esté equivocado' → 'It is possible that I am wrong' (adịghị 'I be wrong'). N'ime meetings, okwukwe ndoro na-eme ka 'I'd suggest we consider...' n'ime ma ọ bụ 'We should change...'. N'ime ndoro ndoro, okwukwe ndoro na-eme ka 'I see your point, but have we considered...?' (na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro adịghị 'No, that's wrong'). N'ime C1, okwukwe ndoro na-eme ka 'I'm not entirely convinced that...' vs. 'I have reservations about...'.

concept_examples.text: Perhaps we could revisit the proposal with a more flexible timeline.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụ na anaghị m egwu ịgụ maka ihe ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /pərˈhæps wiː kʊd riːˈvɪzɪt ðə prəˈpoʊzəl wɪð ə mɔːr ˈfleksəbl ˈtaɪmlaɪn/

concept_examples.text: It seems that the market trends are shifting toward sustainable solutions.
concept_examples.translation: Nke a na-eme ka ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro nke ndoro ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt siːmz ðæt ðə ˈmɑːrkɪt trendz ɑːr ˈʃɪftɪŋ təˈwɔːrd səˈsteɪnəbl səˈluːʃənz/

concept_examples.text: One could argue that the risks have been underestimated.
concept_examples.translation: Ọ bụ na anaghị m egwu ịgụ maka ihe ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wʌn kʊd ˈɑːrɡjuː ðæt ðə rɪsks hæv biːn ˌʌndərˈestɪmeɪtɪd/

concept_examples.text: I'm not entirely convinced that this approach yields the expected results.
concept_examples.translation: A na-emeghị m mma na ihe ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪm nɑːt ɪnˈtaɪərli kənˈvɪnst ðæt ðɪs əˈproʊtʃ jiːldz ði ɪkˈspektɪd rɪˈzʌlts/

common_error.wrong: I think that this is a bad idea.
common_error.correct: I'm not entirely convinced that this is the most effective approach.
common_error.correct_alt: I have some reservations about this approach.
common_error.explanation: Error bụ na-eme ka 'I think' + adjective negative direct, nke na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro dị ka ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro. Ndoro ndoro na-eme ka 'creo que es una mala idea', mana n'ime English, okwukwe ndoro na-elekwa ndoro ndoro nke na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro adịghị adị. Iji wepụta ya, na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro dị ka 'I'm not entirely convinced', 'I have reservations', ma ọ bụ 'Have you considered...?'. N'ihi na 'I think' na-eme ka okwukwe bụ ndoro dị ka 'I believe' ma ọ bụ 'I would argue' n'ime contexts nke ndoro.

examples.original: Could you possibly send me the report by tomorrow?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː ˈpɑːsəbli send miː ðə rɪˈpɔːrt baɪ təˈmɑːroʊ/
examples.translation: Ị nwere ike ịnye m ugwo ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro?
examples.note: Na-eme ka 'could' + 'possibly' na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro adịghị adị ma ọ bụ 'can'.

examples.original: I would appreciate it if you could review this document at your earliest convenience.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd əˈpriːʃieɪt ɪt ɪf juː kʊd rɪˈvjuː ðɪs ˈdɑːkjumənt æt jʊr ˈɜːrliɪst kənˈviːniəns/
examples.translation: A na-akwụ ụgwọ m ka ị ga-eme ka ndoro ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro.
examples.note: Ntụgharị ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro.

examples.original: Would you mind taking a quick look at the proposal?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd juː maɪnd ˈteɪkɪŋ ə kwɪk lʊk æt ðə prəˈpoʊzəl/
examples.translation: Ị na-eme ka ị ga-eme ka ndoro ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro?
examples.note: 'Would you mind' na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro adịghị adị ma ọ bụ gerund (-ing) nke ndoro nke ndoro.

examples.original: I see your point, but have we considered the financial implications?
examples.phonetic: /aɪ siː jʊr pɔɪnt bʌt hæv wiː kənˈsɪdərd ðə faɪˈnænʃəl ˌɪmplɪˈkeɪʃənz/
examples.translation: A na-akwụ m ndoro nke ị na-eme, mana anyị na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro?
examples.note: Na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro ma ọ bụ ndoro nke ndoro.

examples.original: I'm not entirely sure that aligns with our current strategy.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm nɑːt ɪnˈtaɪərli ʃʊr ðæt əˈlaɪnz wɪð aʊr ˈkɜːrənt ˈstrætədʒi/
examples.translation: A na-emeghị m mma na ihe ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro.
examples.note: Na-eme ka 'not entirely sure' na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro adịghị adị.

examples.original: With all due respect, I think there might be another angle to explore.
examples.phonetic: /wɪð ɔːl duː rɪˈspekt aɪ θɪŋk ðer maɪt biː əˈnʌðər ˈæŋɡl tə ɪkˈsplɔːr/
examples.translation: N'ụzọ ndoro nke ndoro, m na-akwụ ụgwọ m ka ndoro ndoro ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro.
examples.note: Ntụgharị 'with all due respect' na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro adịghị adị.

examples.original: The data appears to suggest a slight upward trend in sales.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈdeɪtə əˈpɪrz tə səˈdʒest ə slaɪt ˈʌpwərd trend ɪn seɪlz/
examples.translation: Ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro ndoro nke ndoro ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro.
examples.note: Na-eme ka 'appears to' + 'suggest' na-eme ka okwukwe ndoro adịghị adị.

examples.original: It could be argued that the current model is somewhat outdated.
examples.phonetic: /ɪt kʊd biː ˈɑːrɡjuːd ðæt ðə ˈkɜːrənt ˈmɑːdl ɪz ˈsʌmwʌt ˌaʊtˈdeɪtɪd/
examples.translation: Ọ bụ na anaghị m egwu ịgụ maka ihe ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro nke ndoro.

rule:
Maka mkpuru okwu ndoro na ndoro na mkpuru okwu ndoro na ndoro na C1 n'English, ị ga-achọ ka ị na-eme ka mkpuru okwu ndoro na ndoro na mkpuru okwu ndoro na ndoro:
1. **Mkpuru okwu ndoro na ndoro na ndoro na ndoro**: Mkpuru okwu dịka *suggest, imply, illustrate, portray* n'ọnọdụ *show* ma ọ bụ *tell*, na ndoro ndoro (however, moreover, consequently).
2. **Mkpuru okwu ndoro na ndoro na ndoro na ndoro**: *Must* maka ndoro ndoro ndoro, *might/may* maka ndoro ndoro, na *could* maka ndoro ndoro. Ndoro ndoro ndoro na ndoro na ndoro na ndoro na ndoro na ndoro na ndoro.
3. **Mkpuru okwu ndoro na ndoro na ndoro na ndoro**: Mkpuru okwu dịka *in order to, so as to, with the aim of* na *due to, owing to* na *debido a*.
4. **Presente histórico**: Mkpuru okwu dịka *In Chapter 3, the protagonist meets...* n'ọnọdụ *En el capítulo 3, el protagonista se encuentra...*
5. **Estructuras para expresar propósito y causa**: Mkpuru okwu dịka *in order to, so as to, with the aim of* na *due to, owing to* na *debido a*.
